summary: @<name>:<text> now searches one entity type, also without configuration (@task:123 searched all types for task:123 before). The app can decide which entities appear in @ (mentions in tools.json) and order them by view (useMentionContext); derived labels keep every tools.json language.
howTo: Check your users' habits: whenever the text before the first colon after @ is an entity type's label, alias or canonical type, the @ list now searches only that type for the rest (@task:123 searches task for 123; before, every type for task:123). Nothing to configure for that. Derived entity labels now carry every language of languages in .glirastes/tools.json, and derived action labels every language of the tool title (before only en and de); run glirastes tools refresh and review the labels. Without mentions in tools.json and without a mention context the @ list is as before, plus type suggestions while typing after @ when the chat has at least two entity types. To declare sources set mentions.policy to "declared", run glirastes tools check and paste the mention-source-candidate entries you want into mentions.sources. Call useMentionContext({ preferredTypes, presetType }) in a page below the provider to put its entity types first and preset the filter. Give entity labels and aliases per language in .glirastes/chat-interactions.json; new optional locale keys completionCommandsGroupLabel, completionEntityTypesGroupLabel, completionEntityTypeFilterLabel. An own onCompletionSelect should ignore items of type mention-filter. See docs/chat-interactions.md.
